session_covered: US and European sessions of Tuesday 27 October
intro: Covers the US and European sessions of Tuesday 27 October. This is the 09:00 retry after the first attempt was deferred because the US session had not closed; the ASX opens at 10:00.
footnotes: S&P 500 and Nasdaq closes are from FNArena and match other reports; one CBA note quotes S&P +0.8%, which is not used. The Dow is quoted at 52,377.57 (+0.03%) by FNArena and Investing.com.

Brent is the FNArena reference print (US$114.31, -0.88%); CBA reports the futures settlement at US$113.88/bbl, down 1.7%. Gold is the spot print; gold futures settled at US$4,075/oz (+0.9%). Iron ore is the spot print; futures settled flat at US$90.70/t.
The 10-year yield is quoted as 4.99% by FNArena's table and 5.00% in its text.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures are at 8,884, up 18 points (0.20%) per FNArena; Investing.com shows the same level (Dec contract, 8,884) but a larger +0.71% change from a different reference, and TradingView shows 8,881. Applying 0.20% to the prior ASX 200 close of 8,850.10 (up 40.2 points, 0.46%, led by Materials +2.78%) implies an open about 17.7 points higher, near 8,868. The direction matches the risk-on US session.

local_events: ABS September-quarter CPI: NAB and CBA forecast trimmed mean +1.0% q/q (NAB headline +1.2%), with NAB seeing downside risk to trimmed mean; the print shapes the RBA decision on Tuesday 3 November, where markets price about a 60% chance of a 25bp hike.
what_moved: Wall Street rose as AI-related shares rebounded ahead of big-tech earnings and the Fed decision. Chipmakers led, with Broadcom up almost 4% after banks and Blackstone lined up US$63 billion of financing tied to Anthropic's chip purchases, and the Nasdaq outperformed (+1.18%) while the Dow was flat as Boeing fell about 10%. Oil slipped for a second session on Middle East peace-talk hopes but stayed near six-month highs. Sector breakdowns were not available in the sources used; midday AP reporting had technology leading and energy lagging.

news.headline: Fed expected to hold on Wednesday after last month's hike
news.summary: US stocks closed higher ahead of the Federal Reserve decision, with CME FedWatch about 88% for a hold. Markets price at least two more hikes by mid-2027 as inflation indicators stay elevated amid the US-Iran conflict.

news.headline: Record AI debt deal for Anthropic chip purchases
news.summary: Three banks and Blackstone lined up US$63 billion to fund Anthropic's purchase of Broadcom chips, described as the largest AI debt deal on record. Anthropic has also filed for a potentially record IPO.

news.headline: Australian Q3 CPI due today
news.summary: NAB and CBA expect trimmed mean inflation of 1.0% for the quarter, in line with consensus. Markets price about a 60% chance of an RBA 25bp hike next Tuesday.

news.headline: Oil eases but stays near six-month highs
news.summary: Brent fell for a second session on hopes for Middle East peace talks, though the Houthi-Saudi conflict and the US-Israeli war with Iran remain risks. Brent futures settled at US$113.88/bbl.

news.headline: Boeing slides on 737 delay and wider loss
news.summary: Boeing fell roughly 10% after a larger-than-expected adjusted third-quarter loss and a slip in its 737 production target to early 2027, making it the Dow's biggest drag.

news.headline: Meta's record equity raise
news.summary: Meta shares slipped after a record US$97.5 billion equity raise to fund AI spending, even as US capital goods orders rose in September.

news.headline: Metals firm as ASX Materials surge
news.summary: Gold gained about 1.2% to US$4,062/oz, copper rose 1.8% and aluminium about 2% (CBA), while iron ore was flat near US$90.7/t. ASX Materials rose 2.78% on Tuesday.

coming_up: The Fed rate decision is due in the US on Wednesday 28 October (early Thursday 29 October Sydney time), with a hold widely expected. The RBA meets on Tuesday 3 November, the same day as the US midterm elections.
